en: Of this Śrī Mallārī Kavaca mantra: Skanda is the seer (ṛṣi);
the goddess Śrī Mallārī is the deity; Anuṣṭubh is the meter; its application (viniyoga) is for the recitation (japa) of the Śrī Mallārī Kavaca.
I bow to the Lord of Devas, the husband of Mahālasā, the bestower of boons who is affectionate toward his devotees, the crusher of the wicked, and the master of seventy million sages.
For the sake of favoring the gods, residing upon the mountain of precious gems, with a face ever serene— I pay homage to Mallavairin.
I bow to the one who embodies all the gods, the peaceful one, the youthful, the mine of compassion, the primordial Rudra, the Great Rudra, the beloved of Savitṛ and Kapila.
The God who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, adorned with every ornament.
I bow to the destroyer of the asuras, who resembles ten million suns.
I bow to the primordial God, the Great God, the Supreme Lord Mallārī; I praise the Hero, the Auspicious One, the Three-Eyed Lord, who is compassionate toward his devotees.
I bow to the Lord, the protector of the world, who is the supreme light in the form of enjoyment, adorned with a garland of skulls, and bearing the *triśūla* and other weapons.
I bow to Maheśvara, the bestower of boons upon his devotees, who is eternally present as the healer of Mallārī; he who recites this with devotion [attains his grace].
In the forest, in battle, or in a great fortress; from the fear of kings and thieves as well; from Śākinīs, Ḍākinīs, Bhūtas, Piśācas, Uragas, and Rākṣasas;
during the afflictions of planetary influences (grahas) and diseases; and in the face of fears caused by poison and serpents.
"O Mallārī, O Mallārī! By the chanting of the name 'Mallārī,' the sins committed throughout seven lifetimes perish at that very moment."
Whoever recites this constantly at the three times of day goes to the world of Viṣṇu; at the end of the body, they attain that [state] and are honored in all worlds.
Thus, in the Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, in the Kṣetrakhaṇḍa, within the Mallārī-mahātmya.
